title: Comment on “Free forearm flaps for head and neck reconstruction: fewer revisions and flap failures with two venous anastomoses-a 25-year prospective study”
html: In their article “Free forearm flaps for head and neck reconstruction: fewer revisions and flap failures with two venous anastomoses—a 25-year prospective study”, Kuijpers et al.1 reported that free forearm flaps with one venous anastomosis had significantly higher rates of re-exploration and failure than flaps with two venous anastomoses. They observed re-exploration in 8.3% of one-vein flaps versus 2.8% of two-vein flaps, and flap loss in 6.7% versus 2.0%, respectively. These results underscore that venous outflow is critical to flap survival, as inadequate drainage is a leading cause of free flap failure2.
